title: PPDM table workbench
status: gate met - all seven criteria: bounded server-side paging, server-side filter and sort, edit round-trip preserving untouched columns, optimistically guarded update/delete that reports a conflict, failed read as a failure, row policy predicate applied and surfaced, filtered export. Two limits are recorded: the page's Save/Delete are wired but not covered by an automated UI test, and Insert is available on the gateway only

implementation.page: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop/Views/TableWorkbenchPageView.cs (route 'tableworkbench': grid, filter, sort, paging, detail, export)
implementation.tree: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop/Views/PpdmTreePageView.cs (OpenTableAsync / OpenSelected set the request and navigate)
implementation.shell: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop/Shell/OgShellWindow.xaml.cs (ShowRoute installs the navigator handler and switches page)

integration.table: T_SMOKE_ROW (500 rows, 3 columns, real SQLite through BeepDM)

exportFiltered.note: header + 250 filtered rows + summary line; states 'of 250 matching'

smoke.ppdm-workbench-note: Opening CAT_ADDITIVE in the workbench with filter 'CAT_ADDITIVE'.

gates.AC-1 paging issues a bounded query; 10 0: pass - QueryAsync issues one SELECT with LIMIT/OFFSET, page size is clamped to 500, and a request for 10 000 returned 500. The 500-row SQLite test reads 200/200/100 across three pages.
gates.AC-2 sorting and filtering are server-si: pass - filters and sorts are compiled into WHERE/ORDER BY; a filter on BAND='A' returned exactly the 250 matching rows and a descending ID sort returned 500 then 499.
gates.AC-3 an edit round-trips and preserves u: pass - UpdateAsync writes every non-key column and guards the row on the key plus the original values of the columns written. The opt-in SQLite test edits BAND on ID 1 from B to Z, re-reads and finds BAND Z with DEPTH and ID unchanged. The page exposes Save row (COLUMN value).
gates.AC-4 a concurrency conflict is detected: pass - the guard is a full-row match on the values read, checked before the write; when no row matches, UpdateAsync/DeleteAsync return workbench-conflict. The test reuses a stale original and asserts both the update and the delete are refused with that code while the table keeps its 500 rows, and the page turns that code into a sentence ('Somebody else changed this row...') instead of overwriting.
gates.AC-5 a failed read is never rendered as: pass - the gateway reads the datasource's ErrorObject flag (RunQuery reports provider errors there instead of throwing) and returns a failure with a reference; the page sets a failed view state and the smoke shows workbench-read-failed-not-empty true for CAT_ADDITIVE (absent from the smoke database).
gates.AC-6 row policy is applied and visible: pass - the gateway takes an optional row predicate supplied by the client app (which owns authorization) and ANDs it into every read, so a restricted row is never fetched and the total reflects the policy. The test passes BAND = 'A' and gets exactly 250 of 500 rows, all A, with the note surfaced through PolicyNote and shown in the page's notice line.
gates.AC-7 export respects the active filter: pass - ExportAsync runs the same predicate and writes the filtered rows only: 250 of 500, with the file saying 'of 250 matching'.

limits: The page's Save/Delete buttons and its conflict sentence are wired and compile-verified, but no automated UI test drives a click through them; the round-trip and conflict are proven at the gateway with a real SQLite table.

Insert exists on the gateway and is tested at data level, but the page has no Add row button yet; and the app wires no row predicate today, so AC-6 is proven by test rather than by a real restricted role in the shell.
Reads are `SELECT *` with LIMIT/OFFSET and a separate COUNT; the count is a second query and is not cached.
Column names for a row come from the datasource's entity structure (refreshed once per read); a table the datasource cannot describe falls back to COLUMN_n names.
Search is matched against the metadata registry's key columns only, and is refused when the table has no recorded key.
The smoke's workbench open uses a table absent from the smoke database, so it proves the failed state rather than rendering rows; the row-rendering path is proven by the opt-in 500-row SQLite test.
The grid uses AutoGenerateColumns and is not virtualised; the detail pane is a read-only list of column values, not the DAT-05 form.
